correctness.rationale: The proof was reconstructed independently. For a repeated exponent \(n=p^\alpha m\) with \(m>1\), the Bertrand-prime choice gives \(t\) with \(2t+1\) prime and \(\alpha<3t-2\). The incomparable vertices \(C_{p^t}\) and \(C_{p^{t-1}m}\) cannot have a common lower neighbor because that would give a nontrivial proper divisor of \(2t+1\), and cannot have a common upper neighbor because \(2t-1\mid 2s+1\) forces \(s\ge3t-2>\alpha\). The square-free direction follows from multiplicativity and the universal top vertex. Independent exact graph construction found no counterexample for \(2\le n\le400\).
